blurb: A sqlite Store is created and removed; a PostgreSQL database is connected and disconnected, with a saved login. Default reads use the home's records.
reasons: Why engine: type means file, dir or symlink everywhere else.
Why rows list projects: a project count needs a name for the number; the short list of names answers both.
Why secrets come on stdin: a password in an argument lands in shell history and process listings.
Why connect is not create: LayerFS makes and deletes a sqlite file; a PostgreSQL database exists outside LayerFS and stays when it is disconnected.
Why a saved login without an address: the address is the part that differs per machine and per proxy; the login is the part that is the same everywhere.
Why the auth calls live in store: a top-level layerfs auth would read like logging in to LayerFS itself.
Why move names the destination: push and pull were one operation with two names. store move shop dev sends it; store move shop native brings it back.
Why no default machine on a PostgreSQL Store: no machine owns it. Where a Sandbox runs is chosen at sandbox create.

calls.new_work: A records-only state is new: today each item's state comes from the leases and a `stat` on the Store's machine, and is idle, in_use, busy, down or unresolved. `--machine` is a new filter. `blocked` with `blocked_by` replaces `down`.

calls.note: + store.status, store.stats. state comes from the home's records, with no probe. A sqlite Store is ready, blocked with blocked_by {machine, reason} when its machine is not ready, busy with op {name, phase, started_at} (name is move, remove, compact, backup or restore), or broken with reason unresolved and the clearing call as fix. A PostgreSQL Store is ready, busy or broken; it waits on no machine. Only --with live can answer broken with missing (no file where the record says; the fix restores a backup or removes the Store) or unreachable (this computer cannot reach the PostgreSQL server; the fix is layerfs store doctor <store>), or unknown with observed_at. A sqlite Store answers machine; a PostgreSQL Store answers auth and connections (the one without a machine is the one every machine uses) and has no default machine. The other engine's keys are null in the long form. projects shows the first 20 names. Each backups row is {bucket}, and in the long form {bucket, file, sha256, heads_sha256, last, attempt}: last is the last transfer that worked ({call, at, size}), attempt one that did not ({call, at, error}, else null). heads_sha256 was heads. Whether a machine reaches a PostgreSQL Store is the doctor's to say (store doctor), not this call's

live.help: reads the Store where it lives, starting nothing: a sqlite Store's file through its machine, a PostgreSQL Store's server from this computer; state and its companion then come from the read. holders: the pids of other live processes that hold it; phases: a running compaction's phases in order, else null; behind: the buckets whose backup is older than the Store, null for PostgreSQL; server_version and latency_ms: the PostgreSQL server's answer, null for sqlite

stats.help: opens the Store where it lives. size: the file with its write-ahead log (sqlite), the schema (PostgreSQL); logical_bytes, canonical_bytes, stored_bytes, metadata_bytes: the Store's publication counters; file_bytes: the database's pages; free_bytes: reusable pages, null for PostgreSQL; dedupe and compression: ratios as text, six decimals; init: {entries, files, size, canonical_bytes, stored_bytes, metadata_bytes, duration_ms} of the first project init, or null

calls.new_work: Records-only state with the six states is new: today store.get answers no state and store.status always reads the leases, the file or the server. So that every client sees `busy`, store.compact, backup.create and backup.restore must record an `op` in the Store's record; today only a move and a remove do (a compaction keeps its own record beside the Store, backup.create holds a file lock). `live.behind` is new: it reads the Store's heads where it lives, through its worker on a machine (today backup.list compares them on native only). `attempt` on a backup row is new: today a link is written only after a transfer succeeds. `auth` and `connections` are new (see store.save_auth, store.connect). The reason codes `missing` and `unreachable` replace today's `down_reason` sentence.

calls.note: PostgreSQL. The URL holds host, port, database and TLS options; one with a user or a password is refused InvalidInput. First connect: --auth is required, here and only here; it is made from this computer, which gives an empty database the LayerFS schema and its id, or reads them, and answers the projects found. The URL is the address every machine uses. On a connected Store: with --machine the URL becomes that machine's own address, proven from that machine; without it, it replaces the address every machine uses, proven from this computer. Either must read the Store's id (Unavailable otherwise) and refuses --auth and --synchronous-commit (InvalidInput: a machine never has its own login; both change with store update). A Store has at most one address for every machine and one per machine. A database whose id another Store of this home holds is Exists. projects shows the first 20 names. A running Sandbox keeps its route

calls.note: the Store, in this order: store.record, store.operation (no half-finished move, no stale lease), store.connection (it is reached where it lives), store.identity (the id in its data against the record), store.schema; then a shallow check of each project (project.listed: its record against the Store's own list; a notice with a fix, not an error). It stops after the schema check and reads no data: project doctor --full reads data. A PostgreSQL Store is also probed from each machine that has a Sandbox of it (R9): one store.connection check per machine, with from naming the machine, on the check entry and on its finding. --machine adds a probe from one more machine, Sandbox or not; it is for the command line and is refused InvalidInput for a sqlite Store. Under a stopped machine the records checks are made and the rest are not_checked with blocked_by. The tree is the Store's node with projects. Replaces the off-table layerfs doctor --target store.integrity --name S and --target store.connection, with no alias (R1); --quick and the whole-Store scan it shortened are gone, and so is --timeout. Exits 0 once the report is made

calls.new_work: The call is new on the table. The shallow Store check is new work (C14): today's cheapest Store mode still scans the file, so it needs a cut that stops after the schema check and a new argument on the worker's Store diagnosis that an older worker will not know. Probing a PostgreSQL Store from each machine that has a Sandbox of it is new; the probe itself exists (store.status --machine uses it). `store.schema` and `store.operation` are new check ids; `store.record`, `store.identity` and `store.connection` exist. The project record comparison exists (project.get makes it); reporting it as a notice is new. One answer shape, a time budget per thing and one progress event per finished thing ({phase: self|projects, done, total, node}) are new.
